463a176a36.why: Old tell fixed: the stem no longer defines 'biotic', and the moss (food-chains' producer key) is gone. Pine trees, deer and soil bacteria are all living; 'Producers' is wrong (not all living parts make food) and 'Habitats' is a place. Note only: b91ab91c11's stem teaches 'abiotic = nonliving', which helps a player who meets it first; the cards teach both terms anyway, so not a fail.

b91ab91c11.why: Nectar problem gone: the fly, the pondweed and the bed of weeds are plainly alive, and sunlight and rock are abiotic. Turtles are ectotherms that bask in the sun on rocks and logs; adult frogs eat flies; dabbling ducks eat pondweed and dense pondweed beds shelter fish. The desert lizard-and-hawk scene is gone from this unit. Turtles are a group, not one species, and the fact asked is the abiotic factor, so the lane is clear.

1ff52c5397.why: Lane fixed: no named species now, just a forest's animals in general. The key matches National Geographic's habitat (a home with food, water, shelter and space). 'Its food web' is a live lure, and 'niche' is grade-4 vocabulary in Virginia (SOL 'habitats and niches') and the context defines it. Minor: the context still says 'A den is only shelter', left over from the mountain-lion stem. It is true but names a den that is no longer in the stem.

bb08c5a01e.why: The judge's tell is only moved, not fixed. Every choice now opens with 'Some', but each wrong choice still makes an absolute claim in its second clause ('the rest grow new bodies', 'no new kinds ever move in', 'the plants are unharmed'), so the key is still the only choice with no absolute. Also, 'the plants are unharmed' falls to the stem's own dried pools and baked mud, so only the key and the Lamarck lure are live. The judge's fix (take the absolutes out of the wrong choices) was not applied. The facts are sound: the context's aestivation line is now true.

f6925c3f76.why: 'Trees, stumps and all' is gone; 'clear the ground bare' no longer points at the roots. Key true: roots bind the soil, and deforestation exposes it. 'Rain soaks into bare ground faster' is truly wrong: bare soil seals and soaks up less rain. The nutrients and lighter-soil choices are wrong as reasons, and the context says plainly that the soil's own weight does not change.
